subject: awaitEvent (internal/core/machine/await_test.go), the bounded wait every test of the package uses for an event the code under test must produce (#935)
why: A bare receive on such an event turns a guard that refuses early into a hang until the package timeout, and a falsify verdict cut short that way reads like a mutation with fewer catchers. awaitEvent asks three questions of a wait: did the event come, did it come before the deadline given, and if not, does the failure say what did not happen; one mutation per question, the first two both striking the deadline (unreachable, then early). awaitEventBefore adds three: did the subject return before the event, does the failure then carry the subject's error, and does an event that came win over a return that followed it; one mutation each, and a fourth for a nil return before the event. And one proving a race test does not lean on the helper alone: the subject produced the event, then returned nil without the step. And one on a call site, to show a real early refusal now fails at once with its cause instead of hanging.
